measurements.evidence_location: Characterization of PE and OPE; Fig. 1C
measurements.evidence_quote: Furthermore, the zeta potential became more negative after oxidation, shifting from -53.118 ± 2.918 mV for PE to -63.693 ± 1.803 mV for OPE, reflecting an increase in surface charge density. || C DLS and zeta potential analysis of PE and OPE particles in aqueous dispersion. || the pH of PE and OPE suspensions was measured under the same experimental conditions used for zeta potential analysis. || PE and OPE showed similar mean pH values of 7.3 and 7.6, respectively (Fig. 1D) || The sizes of the PE and OPE particles were measured using a Zetasizer Nano ZSP (Malvern Panalytical, United Kingdom), and their surface charges were also determined with the same device.
